title: Polariton-Assisted Inelastic Tunneling through a Quantum Well
authors: Théophile Seck, Yanko Todorov, Guido Pupillo, David Hagenmüller
abstract: We investigate electronic transport through a doped quantum well strongly interacting with a photonic mode confined in a double-metal cavity. Using a nonequilibrium Green's function formalism, we derive compact expressions for the current valid for arbitrary collective light--matter coupling strengths exceeding the relevant loss rates. We show that cavity polaritons leave observable transport signatures when the carrier injection rate is smaller than the cavity-induced electronic broadening. In this regime, the current--voltage characteristics exhibit inelastic sidebands associated with resonant and anti-resonant polariton emission, which are strongly enhanced under resonant illumination. Our results provide a realistic route to detecting cavity-induced modifications of charge transport in semiconductor heterostructures.
summary: This paper theoretically analyzes electronic tunneling through a quantum well strongly coupled to an optical cavity mode. Using non-equilibrium Green's functions, the authors predict that polariton interactions manifest as distinct inelastic sidebands in the current-voltage characteristics. This offers a powerful spectroscopic tool for characterizing light-matter coupling in semiconductor heterostructures.
main_problem: The study investigates electronic transport through a quantum well strongly coupled to a cavity photon mode, aiming to detect observable signatures of polariton effects in charge current.
main_result: The current-voltage characteristics exhibit inelastic sidebands associated with resonant and anti-resonant polariton emission, providing a realistic detection route for cavity-induced modifications of charge transport.
method: The analysis employs the non-equilibrium Green's function (NEGF) formalism within the Meir–Wingreen framework to derive compact expressions for the current.
model_or_system: The system consists of a doped quantum well coupled to the fundamental TM mode of a double-metal cavity. The interaction is described by a Hamiltonian including electronic, cavity, and light-matter coupling terms.
key_observables: Current–voltage characteristics ($J$-$V$), inelastic sidebands associated with polariton emission ($\omega_\pm$).
important_parameters: Strong coupling regime (coupling strength > loss rates), slow-injection regime (carrier injection rate < electronic broadening).
main_assumptions: The calculations rely on the NEGF formalism, utilizing approximations like the polariton-pole approximation and pseudo-equilibrium assumptions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate $J$-$V$ characteristics showing additional inelastic peaks when coupling is non-zero, comparing coupled vs. uncoupled transport.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the Hamiltonian and using NEGF to derive current expressions; it then applies approximations like the polariton-pole model to calculate radiative self-energies ($\Sigma_{	ext{rad},n}$) and finally derives separate elastic ($J_{	ext{el}}$) and inelastic ($J_{	ext{in}}$) current components.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges concepts from cavity QED (polaritons, strong coupling) with open quantum system transport theory (NEGF), providing a concrete theoretical framework for observing light-matter interaction effects in solid-state electronics.
